interface.signature: logistic_map(width: int, height: int, x_coords: list[int], y_coords: list[int]) -> list[list[int | None]]

preconditions.expression: isinstance(width, int) and isinstance(height, int) and width > 0 and height > 0
preconditions.description: width and height are positive integers defining the map dimensions.

preconditions.expression: isinstance(x_coords, list) and isinstance(y_coords, list) and len(x_coords) == len(y_coords)
preconditions.description: x_coords and y_coords are lists of equal length representing supply point coordinates.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height for x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords))
preconditions.description: All supply points lie within the map boundaries [0, width) x [0, height).

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == height and all(len(row) == width for row in return_value)
postconditions.description: The result is a 2D array with dimensions height x width.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[y][x] is None for x in range(width) for y in range(height)) if len(x_coords) == 0 else True
postconditions.description: If no supply points exist, every cell contains None.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[y][x] == min(abs(x - sx) + abs(y - sy) for sx, sy in zip(x_coords, y_coords)) for x in range(width) for y in range(height)) if len(x_coords) > 0 else True
postconditions.description: If supply points exist, each cell contains the Manhattan distance to the nearest supply point.
